questions.problem: Let $A$ be a $m\times n$ matrix. What is the image of ${R}^{m}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${A}^{T}$ is a $n\times m$ matrix.

Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{m}$ by ${A}^{T}$ gives a linear combination of the columns of ${A}^{T}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ {a}_{1}^{T} & {a}_{2}^{T} & ⋯ & {a}_{m}^{T} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{T}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{m}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{1}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{2}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{m}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{m}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{m}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}$ must be $\text{Col}({A}^{T}),$ the row space of $A.$

questions.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ for all compatible matrices $A$ and $B?$

I. $\text{Null}(A+B)$

II. $\text{Col}(A+B)$

III. $\text{Null}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ is the row space of $({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})^{T}=A+B.$ This consists of all linear combinations of the rows of $A+B.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of $A+B,$ it must be orthogonal to each row of $A+B.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by $A+B,$ we actually multiply each row of $A+B$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ must be orthogonal to the null space of $A+B,$ which is $\text{Null}(A+B).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

questions.problem: Let $A$ be a $4\times 6$ matrix. What is the image of ${R}^{4}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${A}^{T}$ is a $6\times 4$ matrix.

Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ by ${A}^{T}$ gives a linear combination of the columns of ${A}^{T}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {a}_{1}^{T} & {a}_{2}^{T} & {a}_{3}^{T} & {a}_{4}^{T} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{T}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{1}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{2}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{3}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {a}_{4}^{T} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{4}$ under the action of ${A}^{T}$ must be $\text{Col}({A}^{T}),$ the row space of $A.$
